guidance.service: The product the ticket is about. The Support queue receives mail for RiCH and for OLE5, and the ticket does not say which: decide from the content. RiCH is the SMS platform (sending, delivery reports, sender names, message approval, balance, API and integration); OLE5 is administrative correspondence. When it gives you nothing to go on, choose the likelier one and set confidence to low -- that is what tells the reviewer you were guessing.
guidance.queue:
Where the ticket goes when it leaves the Support queue. Decide it first, before you think about how to reply. Choose on what the ticket is about -- not on whether you can answer it, and not on how much the customer told you; even a ticket too vague to act on is about something. Set it on every ticket, whatever the action.

The team scopes at the end describe what each team handles and where the lines between them fall; choose by them. A ticket reporting something broken belongs with the team that can fix it even when you cannot diagnose it. When a ticket is too vague to place, choose the queue its subject points at and set confidence to low. queue_reason says why this queue rather than the others; if you cannot give a reason, you have not chosen.
guidance.next_state: What happens to the ticket next. Waiting For Customer Response when you ask the customer for something; Waiting for Concerned Department when you route; open when you answer. The other states are set by people, not by you.
guidance.type: What the ticket is -- not how much you know about it. A service that is down is Incident / Urgent and a defect is Issue / Problem whether or not you can say why; not knowing the cause is normal, and is what missing and the routing are for. It does not make a fault an Inquiry: keep Inquiry for tickets that actually ask a question.
guidance.subtype: The specific kind of request, from the RiCH branch. Choose the one that names the same thing the ticket reports. When none fits, choose Other -- a near miss misleads the team more than Other does.
guidance.priority: The severity of the problem: judged from the impact on the customer's work -- how many of their messages or users are affected, whether sending stops altogether, whether a workaround exists -- not from the tone. Capitals or the word urgent in a ticket are not impact; a polite ticket reporting that no messages are being delivered is still Critical. Problems outside production, such as a test account, are Low. When it is genuinely unclear, choose 1. Low.
guidance.sla: The service level the ticket is held to. Choose the level with the same severity as the priority you chose: a Critical problem is held to the Critical SLA, a Low one to the Low SLA.

service.description: The RiCH SMS platform: sending messages, delivery reports, sender names, message approval, balance, the API and integrations. Almost every ticket here.

Administrative correspondence (Ole5, معاملاتي / الاتصالات الإدارية): correspondence, inbox, delivery statements, stickers, archive. Another product: always route an OLE5 ticket; it is not ours to answer.

queue.description: Help using RiCH as it works today: sender name registration and renewal (documents, submission to the network providers), delivery checks with the operators (Sent but not Delivered, OTP delays), explaining blacklist/whitelist channels, message parts and throttling, and reports from the portal. The first line for questions.

Changes in the platform or the customer's account: whitelisting IPs and users, creating or changing accounts and API/SMPP/email-to-SMS access, adding or moving balance already approved, template approval, configuration, backend report extractions, operator incidents and rerouting traffic.
Long technical work over days or weeks: VPN and IPsec tunnels, dedicated links, disaster recovery drills, root cause and post-incident reports, archived SMS reports that must be decrypted.
Every ticket from Al Rajhi Bank or a vendor acting for it, whatever the topic: OTP delays, operator incidents, MQ/ESB/SMPP connections, push notifications, DR exercises, notification lists, balance.

The product itself: defects that need a code fix, new features and change requests, whether a behaviour is by design, API specifications and limits, security and compliance questionnaires (SAMA, NCA, penetration tests).
The relationship and the money: contracts, buying balance and top-ups, refunds, Farabi requests before a whitelist or balance change, meetings, training, formal letters, complaints and escalations.
Spam, advertising and mail unrelated to our products only; never a customer request.

next_state.description: Only for junk sent to the Junk queue. Never for a real customer's ticket, even one you have answered completely: they may write back, and a person closes it once they are sure.
When you answer and nothing further is awaited from anyone.
Set by people, not by you: the ticket closes by itself after a waiting period.
Set by people, not by you: a reminder to come back to the ticket later.
When you route: the ticket waits for the team of the queue you chose.
When you ask the customer for something (ask_more): the ticket waits for their answer.
Set by people, not by you: the fix depends on an outside provider and the ticket waits on them.

type.description: A question: how to do something, what something means, what the status of something is. Only for tickets that actually ask a question.
Asks us to do routine work: register or renew a sender name, whitelist an IP or username, add balance, extract a report, change account data.
Something is not working as it should for this customer: an error, messages not delivered, wrong data -- whether or not the cause is known.
Something is down or unusable now for many: sending has stopped, an operator is down, the platform or API is unreachable.
A service we provide failed to be delivered -- messages not sent or delayed -- rather than a screen or feature malfunctioning.
The problem lies with an outside provider, such as a telecom operator or carrier, rather than with RiCH itself.
Asks for something the product does not do yet: a new feature or a change to how it works.
Raised by our own staff for internal work, not by a customer.
Spam, advertising, or mail unrelated to our products. Goes with the Junk queue.
Only when no other type fits at all. Avoid it: it tells the team nothing.

subtype.description: A general question about RiCH that no more specific subtype covers.
A question about what the service offers or how it works.
A request for routine work that no more specific subtype covers.
A request for a report or a data extraction.
A request for something RiCH does not do yet.
A request to change how something works for this customer.
A question about the delivery status of messages: whether they were delivered, the delivery report.
Messages were sent but did not reach the recipients.

priority.description: Low severity: no impact on the customer's sending -- questions, status checks, reports, sender name and routine requests, enhancement requests, problems outside production.
Medium severity: something fails but a workaround exists, or only some messages or users are affected and the work goes on.
High severity: a core function is lost with no acceptable workaround -- many messages not delivered, an important sender or integration stopped -- for this customer.
Critical severity: sending is down or unusable -- no messages go out, the platform or API does not respond.
Not a severity level. A question is 1. Low; do not choose this.
Not a severity level. Do not choose this.
Not a severity level. An enhancement request is 1. Low; do not choose this.

sla.description: For Low severity: questions, requests, enhancements.
